state.question: How many white cars on the same side as {B1} completely pass {B1}?
state.summary: Current evidence supports three distinct white-car passes of the B1/A1 physical track: v1 0-4s shows two white cars in the adjacent lane completing passes of the annotated red vehicle; v2 0-2s corroborates those synchronized passes but does not add a separate count; v2 4-8s shows one additional white car overtaking the same red annotated vehicle on the same side. Because the v2 4-8s interval is disjoint from the v1 0-4s passes and is treated as the same physical B1/A1 track under the synchronized source-frame clock, the best-supported count is 3. Residual uncertainty remains about exact identity/annotation continuity of the v2 4-8s red vehicle, but no further executable observation is required to choose the best-supported option.

review.reason: Evidence confirms two white cars passing in v1 (0-4s) and one white car passing in v2 (4-8s), but does not definitively resolve whether the v2 car is distinct from the v1 cars due to lack of cross-view identity confirmation.

inference_protocol: Video IDs identify the normalized input clips/views and must never be inferred from event or slot IDs.
A reasoning cycle is PLAN -> local FOCUS observation -> memory revision; Reasoner ALIGN may then rebuild the evidence synthesis when useful. Completing one cycle does not imply sufficient evidence.
FOCUS evidence is valid only for its cited video and time span; it cannot prove whole-video or cross-video absence.
Count physical entities or transitions, not frames, mentions, or duplicate observations of the same event.
The final answer must be exactly one option label from the supplied choices, never a video ID, option text, refusal, or unknown.
If residual uncertainty remains when answering, choose the best-supported option label and retain the uncertainty in the summary.
Videos v1, v2 share clock uav-scene-26: equal timestamps/source-frame positions are comparable across these views.
The synchronized UAV views use one source-frame clock; compare equal timestamps across views.
Overlay aliases with the same numeric suffix (for example A1 and B1) denote the same annotated physical track in different views.
A transition seen in both synchronized views is one physical transition, not two countable events.
In this UAV dataset vocabulary, cycles means two-wheeled road vehicles such as bicycles, e-bikes, scooters, motorcycles, and mopeds; count vehicles rather than riders.

A conditional trigger such as when/after/once establishes the synchronized target timestamp; evaluate the requested relation at that time rather than applying the trigger predicate to counted targets.
The following reference-track sidecar covers only annotated aliases already drawn in the proxy videos; it is not a list of countable targets.
A1/B1 is source_track=17; declared=car; A1_visible=0-189 (0.000-6.333s)/300_frames; B1_visible=0-97 (0.000-3.267s)/300_frames.
